generated_from: rule-based decide_round_bid() labels through the v5 dispatch, no model involved
scale_decision: deliberate v5 scaling decision: every one of the 50,000 v5 orders is used, not v4's ~3,000-order experimental sample
split_rule: order-id disjoint, the global v5 split shared by every stage, mode and the supervisor
stop_rule: an auction closes when a round brings no valid improvement, or at the round cap
tie_break: earliest arrival wins an identical offer, roster order offline
minimum_bid_rounding: ceil_to_cents via reverse_auction.agent_minimum_bid, shared by prompt and floor block
examples_per_pair: one, rounds rotating over the rounds the replay ran
round_1_label: asserted equal to the sealed decision at build time

platform_minimum_decrement.schedule: every second order at the default, the rest at 5/10/20% of that stage's opening best bid
platform_minimum_decrement.note: bidding_modes documents the default as a EUR amount; it is a platform rule rather than a sourced price, so v5 applies the same number in the order's currency, USD

categories.auction_round: the replayed round at the price the auction produced
categories.floor_boundary: constructed current_best_bid putting the next offer one percent above, exactly at, and one cent below the agent's minimum_bid, inside the main corpus as in v4

floor_pairs_basis: v4's committed set used --floor-pairs 500 over 3,000 orders, one pair per six orders; v5 keeps that rate over its pool
logistics_floor: a v5 logistics price carries no margin, so minimum_bid is the opening offer and every logistics auction closes after round 2 with all round-2 rows NO_BID
